'''Li Cai''' ({{zh|c=蔡力|p=Cài Lì}}; born c. 1980) is an American [[statistician]] and [[Quantitative psychology|quantitative psychologist]]. He is a professor of Advanced Quantitative Methodology at the [[UCLA Graduate School of Education and Information Studies]] with a joint appointment in the quantitative area of the [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] Department of Psychology. He is also Director of the [[National Center for Research on Evaluation, Standards, and Student Testing]], Managing Partner at [https://www.vpgcentral.com/about/people/li-cai/ Vector Psychometric Group].

He invented the [[Metropolis–Hastings algorithm|Metropolis–Hastings]] [[Stochastic approximation#Robbins.E2.80.93Monro algorithm|Robbins–Monro]] algorithm for [[Statistical inference|inference]] in [[High-dimensional statistics|high-dimensional]] [[latent variable model]]s that had been [[Computational complexity theory#Intractability|intractable]] with [[Expectation–maximization algorithm|existing solutions]]. The algorithm was recognized as a [[Rigour#Mathematics|mathematically rigorous]] breakthrough in the "[[curse of dimensionality]]" and garnered numerous [[Impact factor|top-tier]] publications and national awards.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.1007/s11336-009-9136-x|title = High-dimensional Exploratory Item Factor Analysis by a Metropolis–Hastings Robbins–Monro Algorithm| journal=Psychometrika| volume=75| pages=33–57|year = 2010|last1 = Cai|first1 = Li|url=https://escholarship.org/content/qt3hx0175j/qt3hx0175j.pdf?t=l7nx98|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.3102/1076998609353115|title = Metropolis-Hastings Robbins-Monro Algorithm for Confirmatory Item Factor Analysis| journal=Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics| volume=35| issue=3| pages=307–335|year = 2010|last1 = Cai|first1 = Li|s2cid = 122919429}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=http://lcai.bol.ucla.edu/cv.html | title=My CV}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.aera.net/Division-D/Awards/Outanding-Quantitative-Dissertation | title=Outanding Quantitative Dissertation}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ncme.org/ncme/NCME/About/Awards/Brenda_Loyd_Award/NCME/About1/AwardsFolder/Loyd_Award.aspx |title=Loyd Award |access-date=2017-03-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316120420/https://www.ncme.org/ncme/NCME/About/Awards/Brenda_Loyd_Award/NCME/About1/AwardsFolder/Loyd_Award.aspx |archive-date=2017-03-16 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Career==
A native of [[Nanjing|Nanjing, China]] and alumnus of the [[Nanjing Foreign Language School]], Cai earned a bachelor's degree with distinction from [[Nanjing University]] in 2001. He completed his undergraduate studies in three years and, in that time, also won multiple international competitions for [[public speaking]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.nfls.com.cn/_t6/09/e2/c502a2530/page.htm | title=南大校友获美国"青年科学家总统奖",他告诫学子：认清自己更有益（现代快报）}}</ref> After earning a master's degree in [[journalism]] at [[Ohio State University]] in 2003, he moved to the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], earning a second master's in [[mathematical statistics]] in 2006 and PhD in [[quantitative psychology]] in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sfs.nju.edu.cn/show.php?catid=320&id=249 |title=南京大学外国语学院 |access-date=2017-03-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316114323/http://www.sfs.nju.edu.cn/show.php?catid=320&id=249 |archive-date=2017-03-16 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He joined the psychology and education faculty at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 2008 and was awarded tenure in 2011. He was appointed a full professor in 2014.

==Research==
Cai publishes methodology in [[statistics]] (including [[Computational statistics|statistical computing]]) and [[psychometrics]], and conducts applied research in [[educational measurement]], [[Outcomes research|health outcomes]], and [[developmental psychology]]. He serves on the editorial boards of various journals in quantitative methods in the social sciences.

==Software==
Cai develops flexMIRT, a statistical program for [[multilevel model]]ing and multidimensional [[item response theory]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.vpgcentral.com/software/irt-software/ |title=FlexMIRT® – Vector Psychometric Group |access-date=2017-03-16 |archive-date=2017-03-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316115154/https://www.vpgcentral.com/software/irt-software/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In addition, he is the coauthor (with [[David Thissen]], his doctoral advisor) of IRTPRO, another program for parametric estimation and test scoring.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.ssicentral.com/irt/ | title=SSI - Scientific Software International, Inc | access-date=2017-03-16 | archive-date=2017-05-05 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170505040136/http://www.ssicentral.com/irt/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>
